# Agents Platform Runners
Reports which CLI runners (`claude`, `codex`, `copilot`, `cursor-agent`) are installed on this workspace, and registers them with `agents-platform-multitenant`'s Runners registry so agent model configs can reference this workspace's runners.

Registration is **idempotent** — clicking it again updates the existing entries instead of creating duplicates (dedup key: workspace + CLI).

widgets.title: Requirements
items: agents_platform_token is obtained automatically at activation and refreshed on a half-life schedule — set it by hand in Settings only to override with a different token

agents_platform_base is resolved automatically (agents-platform.<your workspace domain>, or the public agents-platform.aw.tekflox.com) — set it by hand in Settings only to point at a different agents-platform-multitenant instance

widgets.value:
### Notion Kanban webhook (step 4 — manual)

The Ready-card sweep above already picks up Ready cards every `kanban_sweep_interval_s` (60s by default, on by default from first install) — you do not need the webhook below for Ready cards to work. A push-based webhook can replace the sweep's polling delay with a near-instant one, but its *last* step can only be done by hand: Notion has no API to register a webhook subscription (developers.notion.com/reference/webhooks).

1. Open [notion.so/profile/integrations](https://www.notion.so/profile/integrations) → the integration whose secret is saved in the **Notion** app's Settings.
2. Go to its **Webhooks** tab → **Create a subscription**, and point it at this tenant's agents-platform-multitenant `/api/notion/webhook` endpoint.
3. Notion sends a one-time `verification_token` delivery to that endpoint automatically — no action needed for that part.
4. Copy the **Subscription ID** Notion's dashboard shows you (not the token) and paste it below, then click **Register mapping**. This is the automatable half: without it, agents-platform-multitenant refuses every delivery with 404 even after step 2 — it has no way to tell which Notion workspace/integration a subscription belongs to until this mapping exists. `workspace_id`/`integration_id` are looked up automatically from this workspace's own Notion connection; you only ever provide the subscription id.
